text:
Sofia (sales): FYI — Vigilant Health wants to run a 3-week POC to validate their "Vigilant-Med-30B-ft" model for our catalog. They asked about onboarding steps, perf expectations, and what we need for a private deployment. Can we assemble a quick presales checklist?
Ravi (SE): noted. couple clarifying q's: is the artifact a full hf checkpoint or LoRA adapters on top? what tokenizers? target sequence lengths?
Sam (Vigilant Health): it's a 30B PyTorch model + 2 LoRA adapters (diagnosis + discharge-summary). uses a custom sentencepiece vocab with 5 extra tokens. primary workloads are 2k and occasional 12k contexts. prefer Private (VPC) with BYOK.
Anya (solutions): OK. proposed compatibility steps: 1) validate tokenizer -> ensure the 5 custom tokens map and don't get split 2) test LoRA fusion path (fuse adapters -> safetensors shards) 3) run 2k and 12k generate profiles to measure KV cache and memory growth 4) sanity-run on staging dedicated nodes and measure p95 per-token latency.
Ravi (SE): adding: check fp16 -> int8 quant path (we usually recommend PTQ with 4-bit QLoRA-friendly flow). also verify that LoRA fusion doesn't change token offsets for the special tokens.
Ravi (SE): sample upload + compat-run (staging):
```
curl -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/models/upload \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TEST" \
  -F "artifact=@vigilant_med_30b.tar.gz" \
  -F "meta=@meta.json" \
  -F "samples=@vigilant_samples.zip"
```
Anya (solutions): I'll prepare a short estimator for Dedicated vs Hosted for their expected traffic (steady 100 rps, bursts to 400). rough note: if most requests are <512 tokens, hosted can be cheaper; if many 12k contexts, Dedicated or Private with bigger memory nodes likely better.
Liam (security): security intake: we need completed vendor questionnaire + data flow diagram + KMS details + SOC2 attestation. Sam, does Vigilant require we disable analytics/aggregated logging for PHI?
Sam (Vigilant Health): yes — PHI must not leave VPC, and logs must be redacted. BYOK for key wrapping and cloud HSM preferred.
Liam (security): understood. please fill: https://redwood.internal/secques/vigilant (sections A,B,C). we'll also need a contract addendum for PHI handling.
OpsBot: scheduled model-conversion job #conv-8842 for 2025-05-12T06:30:00Z (staging). Estimated run time 1h15m.
Ravi (SE): perf expectation ballpark: 30B with fused LoRA on A100 GPUs, int8 -> p95 token latency ~90-140ms for sequences ~512; 12k contexts will be dominated by KV memory and could push end-to-end request latency into seconds for full-context calls. We'll provide measured numbers after staging runs.
Anya (solutions): fallback strategy: propose routing non-PHI workloads to a smaller distilled variant (redwood-med-13b) when Dedicated capacity is exhausted. PHI-tagged requests get strict VPC-only routing to Private nodes. Sam: is that acceptable?
Sam (Vigilant Health): acceptable for non-sensitive queries. for anything PHI-labeled, must remain on Private nodes. also need committed capacity options and a trial credit for the POC.
Sofia (sales): will draft the commercial note: 3-week POC, recommended staging tests, commit-tier options, and an initial SLA ask (Sam requested 95p token latency ~80ms). we'll caveat based on sequence length.
Liam (security): also will draft enforcement rule: PHI metadata -> route policy = "private-only"; disable external telemetry for those requests. will loop in legal for the addendum.
Ravi (SE): please include at least 10 tokenization examples (plain -> tokenized) in the samples so we can spot mismatches. also include a heavy 12k document to stress KV.
Sam (Vigilant Health): uploading samples & artifact now, adding tokenization examples and sample labels (PHI vs non-PHI).
Anya (solutions): owners: artifact + samples (Sam), compat & perf tests (Ravi), pricing + commit options (Anya), security intake + addendum (Liam), sales deck update (Sofia). ETA: samples today, tests start tomorrow, initial perf + pricing by EoW.
Sofia (sales): perfect — I'll post a short checklist and calendar invite for a Tuesday sync. thanks team! :handshake:
